title: Experimental Schizophrenia-Like Symptoms
author: Max Rinkel, H. Jackson DeShon, Robert W. Hyde, and Harry C. Solomon
summary: Rinkel and colleagues at Boston Psychopathic Hospital administered microgram doses of LSD tartrate to normal volunteers and schizophrenic, depressive, and paranoid patients. They reported the drug reliably produced thought disorder, hallucination, and depersonalization resembling clinical schizophrenia.
citation: Max Rinkel, H. Jackson DeShon, Robert W. Hyde, and Harry C. Solomon, "Experimental Schizophrenia-Like Symptoms," American Journal of Psychiatry 108, no. 8 (February 1952): 572–578.

draft.rationale: The founding paper of the American model-psychosis LSD research tradition (Boston Psychopathic Hospital), distinct from the Saskatchewan psychotherapeutic and biochemical schools already represented in the archive. Rinkel had brought LSD back from a 1949 European trip, and this paper, alongside Stoll's 1947 study, launched the American "experimental" or "model psychosis" school that treated LSD chiefly as a tool for inducing reversible schizophrenia-like states rather than as a psychotherapeutic agent.
